results.title: Normalized Hamming distance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ and permutations $\sigma$, $\tau$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Hamming distance $d_n(\sigma, \tau)$ is the number of points $i < n$ with $\sigma(i) \ne \tau(i)$, divided by $n$, as a real number. For $n = 0$ it is $0$; this single value does not affect statements about limits as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Almost-homomorphisms to symmetric groups

results.summary: Let $G$ be a group and, for each natural number $n$, let $f_n \colon G \to S_n$ be an arbitrary map, where $S_n$ is the group of permutations of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The sequence $(f_n)$ is an almost-homomorphism when for all $g, h \in G$ the normalized Hamming distance $d_n(f_n(g) f_n(h), f_n(gh))$ tends to $0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Closeness to homomorphisms

results.title: Permutation stability

results.title: Metabelian groups

results.title: Minimum palindromic base
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $N$, $b(N)$ is the smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which $N$ is a palindrome, that is, in which the base-$b$ digits of $N$ read the same forwards and backwards. Such a base exists: $0$ has no digits and is a palindrome in every base, and for $N \ge 1$ the number $N$ is written with the single digit $N$ in base $N + 1$.

results.title: Binomial form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $N$ has a base-$b$ representation in binomial form if there are natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ such that the base-$b$ digits of $N$, from the most significant to the least significant, are $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$.

results.title: The minimum palindromic base of two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which the number $2$ is a palindrome is $b(2) = 3$: in base $2$ the number $2$ is written $(1, 0)_2$, which is not a palindrome, while in base $3$ it is the one-digit palindrome $(2)_3$.

results.title: The binomial form of 2023 in base 16
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The number $2023$ has a base-$16$ representation in binomial form: its base-$16$ digits are $7, 14, 7$, that is $7\binom{2}{2}, 7\binom{2}{1}, 7\binom{2}{0}$.

results.title: Brown's theorem on minimal palindromic base one less than the number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $N \ge 1$ be a natural number and let $b(N)$ be the smallest base $b \ge 2$ in which $N$ is a palindrome. If $b(N) = N - 1$, then $N \in \{3, 4, 6\}$, or $N > 6$ and $N$ is prime.

results.title: Digits of a multiple of a power of one more than the base
results.caption: Theorem

Then the base-$b$ representation of $\alpha(1 + b)^k$ has exactly the $k + 1$ digits $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$, from the most significant to the least significant.

results.title: Sufficient condition for a binomial form of a power of 2

results.title: Bases of binomial forms of powers of 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$, $b \ge 2$, $\alpha \ge 1$ and $k \ge 1$ be natural numbers. If the base-$b$ digits of $2^n$, from the most significant to the least significant, are $\alpha\binom{k}{k}, \alpha\binom{k}{k-1}, \dots, \alpha\binom{k}{0}$, then $b = 2^x - 1$ for some natural number $x \le n$, and $\alpha = 2^i$ for some natural number $i$.

results.title: Even-length palindromes are divisible by the base plus one

results.title: Even-length palindromic powers of 2 have base one less than a power of 2
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $n$ and $b \ge 2$ be natural numbers. If the base-$b$ representation of $2^n$ is a palindrome with an even number of digits, then $b = 2^x - 1$ for some natural number $x$.

results.title: Three-digit palindromic powers of two
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Three-digit binomial forms of powers of two

results.title: Even-length palindromic prime powers have base one less than a power of the prime
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Digits of a power of the base and of its successor
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Infinitely often
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, the ω-language “infinitely often $p$” consists of the infinite words $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ with $x_k \in p$ for infinitely many $k$.

results.title: Eventually always
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, the ω-language “eventually always $p$” consists of the infinite words $x_0 x_1 x_2 \ldots$ for which there is an $N$ with $x_k \in p$ for all $k \ge N$.

results.title: Complement of “infinitely often”
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every set $p$ of symbols, the complement of the ω-language of infinite words with infinitely many letters in $p$ is the ω-language of infinite words whose letters are eventually all in the complement of $p$.

results.title: Two-state Büchi automaton for “infinitely often”
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, this is the nondeterministic Büchi automaton over the alphabet of symbols with states $\mathsf{true}$ and $\mathsf{false}$, single start state $\mathsf{true}$ and single accepting state $\mathsf{true}$, in which reading a letter $x$ from either state leads to exactly one state: $\mathsf{true}$ if $x \in p$ and $\mathsf{false}$ otherwise. So the state records whether the last letter read…

results.title: Two-state Büchi automaton for “eventually always”
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $p$ of symbols, this is the nondeterministic Büchi automaton over the alphabet of symbols with states $\mathsf{false}$ and $\mathsf{true}$, single start state $\mathsf{false}$ and single accepting state $\mathsf{true}$. From $\mathsf{false}$ it may read any letter and move to either state; from $\mathsf{true}$ it may read only letters in $p$, and then it stays in $\mathsf{true}$.

results.title: Run-length compression from a pending run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a bit $c$, a natural number $r$ and a finite bit list $w$, the compression $C(c, r, w)$ of $w$ from the pending run $(c, r)$ is the list of natural numbers defined by recursion on $w$. If $w$ is empty, $C(c, r, w)$ is the one-entry list $(r)$. If $w$ is a bit $b$ followed by a list $w'$, then $C(c, r, w)$ is $r$ followed by $C(\lnot c, 1, w')$ when $b \ne c$; it is $255$, then $0$, followed by $C(c, 1, w')$…

results.title: Run-length compression
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The run-length compression of a finite bit list $w$ is $C(0, 0, w)$, the compression of $w$ from an empty pending run of zero bits. It lists the lengths of the maximal runs of $w$, alternating between zeros and ones and starting with a possibly empty run of zeros; a run of length $n > 255$ is written as $255, 0, 255, 0, \dots, 255, 0, m$ with $1 \le m \le 255$.

results.title: Run-length expansion from a starting bit
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a bit $c$ and a list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the expansion $E(c, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$ is the bit list obtained by concatenating, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $n_i$ copies of $c$ when $i$ is odd and $n_i$ copies of $\lnot c$ when $i$ is even.

results.title: Run-length expansion
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The run-length expansion of a list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers is $E(0, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$, the expansion from the zero bit: the bit list obtained by concatenating, for $i = 1, \dots, k$ in order, $n_i$ zeros when $i$ is odd and $n_i$ ones when $i$ is even.

results.title: Compression from a short pending run emits counts at most 255
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit $c$, every natural number $r \le 255$ and every finite bit list $w$, every entry of the compression $C(c, r, w)$ of $w$ from the pending run $(c, r)$ is at most $255$.

results.title: Run lengths fit in 8 bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite bit list $w$, every entry of the run-length compression of $w$ is at most $255$.

results.title: Length of an expansion from a starting bit
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit $c$ and every list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the expansion $E(c, (n_1, \dots, n_k))$ has length $n_1 + \dots + n_k$.

results.title: Length of a run-length expansion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every list $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ of natural numbers, the run-length expansion of $(n_1, \dots, n_k)$ has length $n_1 + \dots + n_k$.

results.title: Expansion recovers the pending run and the input
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every bit $c$, every natural number $r$ and every finite bit list $w$, the expansion from the starting bit $c$ of the compression $C(c, r, w)$ is the list of $r$ copies of $c$ followed by $w$.

results.title: Run-length expansion inverts compression
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite bit list $w$, the run-length expansion of the run-length compression of $w$ is $w$.
